title: The keyboard manager does not work after I restart my computer

judgment.rationale: The manual toggle is a strong signal that initialization is not reapplied after restart. A targeted maintainer repro can test the persisted-state load and hook startup without asking the reporter to perform maintainer profiling.
evidence: Keyboard Manager remaps the Copilot key to Right Ctrl on Windows 11, installed from the Microsoft Store at 0.101.2362.
The toggle remains on after reboot, but the remap does not take effect until toggled off/on.
The report includes a screenshot but no diagnostic ZIP or discussion.

fix_assessment.rationale: A code fix may be applicable to Keyboard Manager startup initialization, but the exact hook/service boundary is not confirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Reapply enabled Keyboard Manager remaps after restart
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The enabled setting persists across restart, but the runtime hook/remap is not reinitialized until the user toggles Keyboard Manager, leaving configuration state and active interception out of sync.
plan: Trace startup loading of the enabled state and the code path used by the manual toggle.
Ensure the same remap/hook initialization path runs after startup once required services and permissions are ready.
Make initialization idempotent and report failures rather than leaving the toggle falsely enabled.
Add restart/persisted-state coverage for the Copilot-to-Right-Ctrl mapping.
verification: Restart with the remap enabled and verify it works before any Settings interaction.
Verify toggling off/on remains correct and that startup failures do not leave a false enabled state.

confidence.rationale: The toggle recovery strongly supports a missed initialization path, but the report does not identify whether the hook, service, or persisted remap load is responsible.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager remains enabled after restart but the Copilot-key-to-Right-Ctrl remap is inactive until the user toggles the feature off and on. The report is reproducible across restarts but lacks startup diagnostics and exact remap state details.
known_information: Keyboard Manager remaps the Copilot key to Right Ctrl on Windows 11, installed from the Microsoft Store at 0.101.2362.

inferences: The persisted enabled state may be loaded before the keyboard hook/driver is ready, leaving a stale runtime state until a manual toggle reinitializes it.
A startup permission, service, or remap-specific issue remains possible.

actions.label: Reproduce Keyboard Manager remap loss after restart

prerequisites: Copilot key remapped to Right Ctrl
steps: Enable the remap and verify the Copilot key produces Right Ctrl.
Restart Windows and confirm the Keyboard Manager toggle still shows enabled.
Test the Copilot key before changing settings.
Toggle Keyboard Manager off and on, then test the key again.
reproduce.expected_result: The remap should work immediately after restart; the current behavior is inactive remapping until the toggle is cycled.
